# Two more shapes RFC 5545 answers on its own.
#
# The first is counting back. Section 3.3.10 states the negative form for BYMONTHDAY,
# BYYEARDAY, BYWEEKNO and BYDAY in one sentence each and section 3.8.5.3 works only the small
# ones — -1SU, -2MO, -3 and -1. The ordinals below count back far enough that the run they
# count within has to have been measured, not assumed: -5MO exists only in a month with five
# Mondays, and -20MO counts back through a year's fifty-two.
#
# The second is a pair of spellings the RFC makes equal. Section 3.8.5.3 prints the same answer
# for the YEARLY and the DAILY spelling of "every day in January, for 3 years", so a rule the
# same sentences make equal to another has the other one's answer whichever way it is written.
# Where an interval skips a stretch of the calendar the recurrence set has nothing there at all,
# which is the same statement asked from the other side.
#
# name | dtstart | rrule | exdates | window start | window end | expected

# Every month has a 28th and no month has more than a 31st, so once the days that do not exist
# are ignored the last of what is left is the last day of the month. February keeps only its
# 28th; a rule listing 29,30,31 alone would give February nothing to select from at all.
BYSETPOS=-1 over 28,29,30,31 is the last day of the month | 19970131T090000 | FREQ=MONTHLY;BYMONTHDAY=28,29,30,31;BYSETPOS=-1 |  | 19970101T000000 | 19980101T000000 | 19970131T090000,19970228T090000,19970331T090000,19970430T090000,19970531T090000,19970630T090000,19970731T090000,19970831T090000,19970930T090000,19971031T090000,19971130T090000,19971231T090000
BYSETPOS=-1 skips the month whose 31st does not exist | 19970331T090000 | FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=1,2,3;BYMONTHDAY=31;BYSETPOS=-1 |  | 19970101T000000 | 20000101T000000 | 19970331T090000,19980331T090000,19990331T090000

# -5MO is the fifth-to-last Monday, which exists in March, June, September and December of 1997
# and in none of the other eight months.
BYDAY=-5MO names only the months with five Mondays | 19970303T090000 | FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-5MO |  | 19970101T000000 | 19980101T000000 | 19970303T090000,19970602T090000,19970901T090000,19971201T090000
# A year holds fifty-two Mondays in each of 1997, 1998 and 1999, so -20MO is the thirty-third.
BYDAY=-20MO counts back through the Mondays of the year | 19970818T090000 | FREQ=YEARLY;BYDAY=-20MO |  | 19970101T000000 | 20000101T000000 | 19970818T090000,19980817T090000,19990816T090000

# Five positive ordinals and a BYSETPOS of -1 name what -1MO names.
five BYDAY ordinals under BYSETPOS=-1 is the last Monday | 19970929T090000 | FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=1MO,2MO,3MO,4MO,5MO;BYSETPOS=-1 |  | 19970901T000000 | 19980301T000000 | 19970929T090000,19971027T090000,19971124T090000,19971229T090000,19980126T090000,19980223T090000
# A weekly rule naming all seven weekdays is a daily rule.
a weekly rule naming all seven days is a daily rule | 19970902T090000 | FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SU,MO,TU,WE,TH,FR,SA |  | 19970902T000000 | 19970912T000000 | 19970902T090000,19970903T090000,19970904T090000,19970905T090000,19970906T090000,19970907T090000,19970908T090000,19970909T090000,19970910T090000,19970911T090000
# A daily rule limited to one month and one day of it is a leap-day rule.
a daily rule limited to February 29 recurs on leap days | 20000229T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;BYMONTH=2;BYMONTHDAY=29 |  | 20000101T000000 | 20090101T000000 | 20000229T090000,20040229T090000,20080229T090000

# Section 3.8.5.3's "Every day in January, for 3 years", both spellings, asked from the middle
# of the second January. UNTIL is 14:00 on January 31st 2000 and the instances are at 09:00, so
# the last day of the last January is in.
every day in January for 3 years, the YEARLY spelling, from mid-January 1999 | 19980101T090000 | FREQ=YEARLY;UNTIL=20000131T140000Z;BYMONTH=1;BYDAY=SU,MO,TU,WE,TH,FR,SA |  | 19990115T000000 | 20000201T000000 | 19990115T090000,19990116T090000,19990117T090000,19990118T090000,19990119T090000,19990120T090000,19990121T090000,19990122T090000,19990123T090000,19990124T090000,19990125T090000,19990126T090000,19990127T090000,19990128T090000,19990129T090000,19990130T090000,19990131T090000,20000101T090000,20000102T090000,20000103T090000,20000104T090000,20000105T090000,20000106T090000,20000107T090000,20000108T090000,20000109T090000,20000110T090000,20000111T090000,20000112T090000,20000113T090000,20000114T090000,20000115T090000,20000116T090000,20000117T090000,20000118T090000,20000119T090000,20000120T090000,20000121T090000,20000122T090000,20000123T090000,20000124T090000,20000125T090000,20000126T090000,20000127T090000,20000128T090000,20000129T090000,20000130T090000,20000131T090000
every day in January for 3 years, the DAILY spelling, from mid-January 1999 | 19980101T090000 | FREQ=DAILY;UNTIL=20000131T140000Z;BYMONTH=1 |  | 19990115T000000 | 20000201T000000 | 19990115T090000,19990116T090000,19990117T090000,19990118T090000,19990119T090000,19990120T090000,19990121T090000,19990122T090000,19990123T090000,19990124T090000,19990125T090000,19990126T090000,19990127T090000,19990128T090000,19990129T090000,19990130T090000,19990131T090000,20000101T090000,20000102T090000,20000103T090000,20000104T090000,20000105T090000,20000106T090000,20000107T090000,20000108T090000,20000109T090000,20000110T090000,20000111T090000,20000112T090000,20000113T090000,20000114T090000,20000115T090000,20000116T090000,20000117T090000,20000118T090000,20000119T090000,20000120T090000,20000121T090000,20000122T090000,20000123T090000,20000124T090000,20000125T090000,20000126T090000,20000127T090000,20000128T090000,20000129T090000,20000130T090000,20000131T090000

# The years and months an INTERVAL steps over hold nothing at all.
a year an INTERVAL of 2 steps over holds nothing | 19970310T090000 | FREQ=YEARLY;INTERVAL=2;COUNT=10;BYMONTH=1,2,3 |  | 19980101T000000 | 19990101T000000 |
a stretch an INTERVAL of 18 months steps over holds nothing | 19970910T090000 | FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=18;COUNT=10;BYMONTHDAY=10,11,12,13,14,15 |  | 19980101T000000 | 19990101T000000 |
